requirements.title: Claude session refuses to start when no executable is resolved
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:83 - guard let executable = configuration.executable else { throw ProviderError.notInstalled(configuration.provider) }
requirements.preconditions: A thread on provider .claude; ProviderRegistry could not resolve an executable so SessionConfiguration.executable is nil.
requirements.expected_result: start() throws ProviderError.notInstalled(.claude) before any process is spawned. Its errorDescription is exactly "Claude is not installed. Install it and sign in with `claude auth login`." (the backticks are part of the string).
failure_cases: This IS the failure path; no further work is done.
requirements.windows_path: Executable resolution is the platform boundary (PA-0010): the bare name "claude" must resolve through PATH plus PATHEXT, where an npm install typically leaves claude.cmd rather than an extensionless file. A failure to resolve must reach this same throw, not a spawn error.
requirements.verification_method: unit test on the session factory with a nil executable, asserting the exact message

requirements.title: Claude session id is the resume id, else a fresh lowercased UUID

requirements.expected_result: id = configuration.resumeID when non-nil (an EMPTY STRING is not treated as nil here, unlike Command Code and Pi), otherwise UUID().uuidString.lowercased(), a lowercase hyphenated UUID. start() returns this id on success.
requirements.persistence: The returned id becomes the thread's provider resume id, stored by the thread runtime, not by this file.
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: UUID generation is platform neutral; the lowercasing must be invariant (ASCII), not locale sensitive.
requirements.verification_method: unit test asserting lowercase form and resume passthrough

requirements.title: Claude probes --help once per executable path for two optional flags and does not cache a failed probe
requirements.preconditions: A resolved executable.
requirements.action: start() asks for the executable's known options.
requirements.expected_result: On a cache hit keyed by executable.path the cached Set is returned and no process runs. On a miss, Shell.run(executable, ["--help"], environment: environment, timeout: 20) runs; ANSI is stripped from result.output + result.errorOutput; the Set is the members of the literal two-element array ["--system-prompt-snapshot", "--forward-subagent-text"] whose text appears in the help output; that Set is cached. If Shell.run throws, the EMPTY set is returned and NOTHING is cached, so the next launch probes again.
side_effects: One `claude --help` child process per executable path, bounded at 20 seconds
requirements.persistence: In-memory static cache for the life of the app process only; nothing on disk.
failure_cases: Probe throws or times out: empty set, not cached, both optional flags omitted for that launch. Behaviour can therefore differ between the first and second launch after a probe failure.
requirements.cancellation: Governed only by Shell.run's 20 second timeout.
requirements.windows_path: Shell.run maps to the Windows process layer (PA-0007, PA-0008). ANSI stripping is load-bearing on Windows because CLIs emit VT sequences into pipes.
requirements.verification_method: unit test with a scripted stand-in emitting help text, then a failing stand-in, asserting the second launch probes again

requirements.title: Claude spawns one line-framed process per thread in the thread's working directory and attaches a reader
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:136-151 - StdioProcess(executable:arguments:directory:environment:), try process.start(), readTask iterating process.messages then didClose()
requirements.preconditions: Argument vector and environment built.
requirements.expected_result: One StdioProcess is created with the executable, the argument array, directory = configuration.workingDirectory and the built environment, with the DEFAULT framing (newline-delimited JSON, not Content-Length). try process.start() propagates a launch failure out of start(). A read Task then consumes process.messages one JSON object at a time calling handle(_:), and calls didClose() when the stream ends. isRunning reports the process's own isRunning.
side_effects: One child process for the life of the thread session
failure_cases: process.start() throwing propagates out of start() unchanged.
requirements.windows_path: The lines framer must split on 0x0A only and tolerate a trailing 0x0D reaching the JSON parser, because the source does not strip CR (port_impacts.md entry 18). The child must be placed in a Job Object so its own children die with it (PA-0007).
requirements.verification_method: interaction test against the scripted Claude stand-in in tests/fixtures

requirements.title: Claude control requests are numbered marrow-<n> from 1 and resolved by exact id match
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:301-309 - control(_:) pre-increments controlCounter, builds requestID = "droppy-code-\(controlCounter)", registers it with `pendingControl.register(requestID)` (a PendingReplies, :37) and inside that registration sends {"type":"control_request","request_id":<id>,"request":<request>}

porting/decision_batch_20260922b.md F1 - every remaining "Droppy Code" / "droppy-code" the app shows or sends out becomes "Marrow" / "marrow", except droppy-code.json and DROPPY_CODE_PROJECT_ROOT (accepted by OD-0012)

The wire object is {"type":"control_request","request_id":"marrow-<n>","request":<the request object>}. The reply is matched on message.response.request_id and resolves that continuation. control() throws ProviderError.notRunning when there is no process, and ProviderError.failed(launchError ?? "Claude exited.") when hasClosed is already true.

OD-0012 F1 renames every remaining "droppy-code" the app sends out to "marrow"; this prefix is not one of its two exceptions (droppy-code.json and DROPPY_CODE_PROJECT_ROOT).

requirements.title: Codex falls back to forking the thread when the server refuses rollback on a paginated thread
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CodexSession.swift:213-215 - catch let error as RPCError where error.message.contains("paginated threads do not support thread/rollback") { return try await forkHistory(...) }
requirements.preconditions: thread/rollback failed with that exact substring.
requirements.expected_result: The fallback fires ONLY on an RPCError whose message contains the substring "paginated threads do not support thread/rollback". With no previousID (the target was the first turn) the original thread is archived with "thread/archive", threadID and turnID are cleared and nil is returned. Otherwise the thread parameters plus "threadId" (the original), "lastTurnId" (previousID) and "excludeTurns" = true are sent as "thread/fork"; the result must carry a string thread.id DIFFERENT from the original, else "Codex did not create a conversation at the revert point." is thrown. The new thread's last turn is then verified with a one-element descending thread/turns/list whose first id must equal previousID and must not equal the target, else "Codex did not confirm the reverted conversation history." is thrown. On success the ORIGINAL thread is archived; on any throw inside that verification block the NEW thread is archived instead with try? and the error is rethrown. Finally threadID becomes the new id, turnID is cleared, activeModel is updated from result.model when present, and the new id is returned.
side_effects: Up to four RPC round trips; one thread archived either way
requirements.persistence: The thread's resume id changes to the forked thread's id, or becomes nil when the whole conversation was archived.
failure_cases: The two exact messages above; a failed verification archives the new thread and rethrows.
requirements.windows_path: None.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test over the fork path, the no-previous path and the verification failure

requirements.title: Codex parses a reset date as epoch seconds, epoch milliseconds above 1e10, or ISO 8601
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CodexSession.swift:467-476 - resetDate: guard let value else { return nil }; if let number = value.double ?? value.string.flatMap(Double.init) { guard number > 0 else { return nil }; return Date(timeIntervalSince1970: number > 10_000_000_000 ? number / 1_000 : number) }; guard let text = value.string else { return nil }; return ISO8601.date(from: text)

DroppyCode/Core/Support/ISO8601.swift:10,:13,:19-21 - static let fractional = Date.ISO8601FormatStyle(includingFractionalSeconds: true); static let plain = Date.ISO8601FormatStyle(); static func date(from text: String) -> Date? { (try? fractional.parse(text)) ?? (try? plain.parse(text)) }
requirements.preconditions: A credit expiry value.
requirements.expected_result: A nil value yields nil. A double, or a string that parses as a double, is rejected when it is not greater than zero; otherwise it is treated as epoch MILLISECONDS when greater than 10000000000 (divided by 1000) and epoch SECONDS otherwise. A non-numeric string is parsed by ISO8601.date(from:): first with Date.ISO8601FormatStyle(includingFractionalSeconds: true), then, on failure, with a default Date.ISO8601FormatStyle(). Anything else yields nil.
failure_cases: An unparseable value yields nil and the credit simply has no expiry.
requirements.windows_path: ISO 8601 parsing must be culture-invariant on Windows; a locale-aware date parser would accept or reject different strings.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over seconds, milliseconds, a fractional ISO string (2026-09-13T18:28:42.057Z), a plain ISO string (2026-09-13T18:28:42Z) and junk
requirements.b2_change: CHANGED (implementation): B1 CodexSession.swift:461-472 parsed the ISO branch with ISO8601DateFormatter using [.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds], then a default ISO8601DateFormatter(). B2 :472 is "return ISO8601.date(from: text)", which tries Date.ISO8601FormatStyle(includingFractionalSeconds: true) then Date.ISO8601FormatStyle() (Core/Support/ISO8601.swift:10,:13,:19-21). The attempt order is the same; whether edge inputs (offsets other than Z, lowercase letters) parse identically under the two APIs is UNKNOWN: nothing was run. Lines 461-472 -> 464-473.

requirements.title: Codex converts a growing cumulative token total into per-update spend for the lead and records it under the lead thread id, naming the most recent turn's model
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CodexSession.swift:597-615 - thread/tokenUsage/updated lead branch with the comment at :603-609: if let total = usage["total"]?["totalTokens"]?.int, total > 0 { let spend = spendTracker.spend(total: total, before: max(0, total - used)); recordCodexSpend(spend, rolloutID: threadID, model: activeModel) } else { recordCodexSpend(used, rolloutID: threadID, model: activeModel) }
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CodexSession.swift:39,:96,:105,:301 - activeModel, set from the thread/start, thread/resume and fork results

DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CodexSession.swift:147-149 - `if let model = input.model ?? activeModel { // A turn can switch the thread's model; the spend it reports is this turn's model's. activeModel = model ...` inside send(), before turn/start is requested
requirements.preconditions: A thread/tokenUsage/updated notification for the lead.
requirements.expected_result: Without a tokenUsage object or its "last" field the notification is ignored. used = last.totalTokens or zero, emitted as .usage(ContextUsage(usedTokens: used, windowTokens: tokenUsage.modelContextWindow)). When tokenUsage.total.totalTokens is an int GREATER than zero, the spend is spendTracker.spend(total: total, before: max(0, total - used)); the `before` seed means a RESUMED thread's first update does not charge its whole history. When the total is absent or not positive, the per-update `used` value is the spend instead. Either way the spend goes to recordCodexSpend with rolloutID = the lead's threadID and model = activeModel: when the spend is positive and threadID is non-empty it is written with TokenLedger.shared.record(codexSpend:rolloutID:), and a .tokenSpend(TokenSpend(provider: .codex, totalTokens: spend, model: activeModel)) event with no agentID is emitted after the .usage event. A zero spend writes and emits nothing. activeModel is not only set from the thread/start, thread/resume and fork results: every send() also sets it to input.model ?? activeModel (when that is non-nil) before requesting turn/start, so a turn that switches the thread's model makes the model of THAT turn, not the model the thread started, resumed or forked with, the one later lead .tokenSpend events and TokenLedger records name.
side_effects: A .tokenSpend event when the spend is positive
A TokenLedger write when the spend is positive and the thread id is known
requirements.persistence: TokenLedger.record(codexSpend:rolloutID:) adds the spend to the day's total and to liveCodex[<rollout id lowercased>], saved by LiveSpendStateStore 2 seconds after the first unsaved record, one delayed write that later records do not push back (PR-PROVCLI-441, TokenLedger.swift:122-145), so the Codex history scan subtracts it from that rollout.
failure_cases: Missing usage: nothing happens.
A nil or empty threadID: the .tokenSpend event is still emitted but nothing is written to the ledger; the history scan owns that usage.
requirements.windows_path: None.

"fileChange": .edit titled with the single relative path, or "Edit <n> files" when there is not exactly one. "mcpToolCall": .mcp titled "<server> · <tool>" defaulting to "MCP" and "tool", detail the compact arguments unless that string is "null". "dynamicToolCall": .other titled item.tool or "Tool". "webSearch": .web titled item.query or "Web search". "collabAgentToolCall": .agent whose verb comes from the table spawnAgent -> "Send out a head", sendInput / sendMessage / followupTask -> "Brief a head", wait -> "Wait for heads", closeAgent / interruptAgent -> "Recall a head", resumeAgent -> "Resume a head", listAgents -> "List heads", default -> "Agent"; the title is the prompt flattened to at most 90 characters when present, with the verb as the detail, else the verb as the title with no detail. "subAgentActivity": nil, deliberately, because as rows they only doubled the head's report pill. "imageView": .read titled with the relative item.path or the literal "Image". "imageGeneration": .other titled item.revisedPrompt or "Generate image". "enteredReviewMode" and "exitedReviewMode": .other titled "Review" with item.review as the detail. Anything else: nil.

requirements.title: Command Code's executable name is the bare cmd, with three alternate names and five directories as fallbacks
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderRegistry.swift:246-259 - the fallback list: which("command-code"), which("commandcode"), which("cmd"), then command-code and cmd under <home>/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, <home>/.npm-global/bin and <home>/.volta/bin
requirements.preconditions: Provider detection is resolving the Command Code CLI.
requirements.expected_result: The primary name is the bare string "cmd". When a custom path is set it is used instead and no fallback is tried. Otherwise PATH is searched for "cmd"; failing that, the fallback list is searched in order and the FIRST executable file wins: which("command-code"), which("commandcode"), which("cmd"), then, for each of <home>/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, <home>/.npm-global/bin and <home>/.volta/bin, the names "command-code" then "cmd". The comment records why: "cmd" is the documented alias and "command-code" and "commandcode" are the package's own names.
requirements.persistence: The resolved path is used for every later spawn.
failure_cases: Nothing resolvable leaves configuration.executable nil, which start() reports as not installed.
requirements.windows_path: THIS IS THE NAMED WINDOWS HAZARD. Resolving the bare name "cmd" through PATH plus PATHEXT on Windows finds C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe, the command interpreter, long before any provider CLI; launching it with this provider's argv would open a console that speaks no protocol on stdout and the session would hang at the first read. UNK-0006 is RESOLVED by PA-0016 (ENGINEERING DECISION): resolution honours PATHEXT, and a candidate whose Windows version resource identifies it as the command interpreter (CompanyName Microsoft Corporation with OriginalFilename Cmd.Exe or Cmd.Exe.MUI, or FileDescription Windows Command Processor), or which is %SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe or %SystemRoot%\SysWOW64\cmd.exe, is rejected. PA-0016 validates identity before any resolution is accepted, so the fallback which("cmd") is checked too. If nothing else resolves, the provider reports not installed, exactly as the source does when nothing is found, and the user can point the existing binaryPath setting at the executable. The fallback directories are macOS and Unix package-manager paths; where an npm or volta install puts the Command Code CLI on Windows is not in the pinned source and stays a live-verification item under PA-0016, which is unverified against a real Command Code Windows install.
requirements.verification_method: PA-0016's Windows contract test: with no Command Code installed, resolution returns not installed rather than System32\cmd.exe, and a stub executable whose version resource does not identify the command interpreter IS accepted; plus a unit test on the fallback order; plus a live Windows probe recording where the CLI actually installs

requirements.title: Command Code rewrites two families of account errors into actionable sentences
requirements.preconditions: A failure error text.
requirements.expected_result: The text is lowercased for the tests. When it contains "not authenticated" OR "unauthorized" OR "session expired", the whole message is REPLACED by "Command Code is not signed in. Run `cmd login` in Terminal, or add a Studio API key in Settings → Providers → Command Code." When it contains "insufficient credits" OR "out of credits", it is replaced by "Command Code is out of credits. Top up at commandcode.ai/billing, or wait for the monthly credits to reset." Both replacements are identical to the exit-code 3 and 10 messages. Otherwise the original text is returned unchanged. Executable identity is validated per PA-0016: PATH resolution honours PATHEXT, and a candidate whose Windows version resource identifies it as the command interpreter (CompanyName Microsoft Corporation with OriginalFilename Cmd.Exe/Cmd.Exe.MUI, or FileDescription Windows Command Processor), or which is %SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe or %SystemRoot%\SysWOW64\cmd.exe, is rejected and the provider reports not installed.

requirements.title: Command Code watches the approvals directory for writes and rescans on every event
requirements.preconditions: A session started.
requirements.expected_result: Any previous watcher is cancelled first. The directory is opened for event notification only; a failure to open leaves NO watcher, and the gate then works only through the scan that tool_queued triggers. A filesystem object source is created for the WRITE event mask, delivering on the main queue, whose handler calls scanApprovals. Its cancel handler closes the descriptor. stopWatcher cancels and clears it.
side_effects: An open file descriptor and a dispatch source for the life of the session
failure_cases: A failed open silently degrades to scan-on-tool-queued only.
requirements.windows_path: There is no equivalent of a write-masked file-descriptor event source; the Windows implementation must use directory change notification for the same directory and deliver on the UI thread, and it must still tolerate missing events, because the source already falls back to an explicit scan at tool_queued. requirements.title: Command Code scans request files in lexicographic order and deletes each as it reads it
requirements.preconditions: A turn is active and an approvals directory exists.

Each is read and parsed; an unreadable or unparseable file is SKIPPED and left in place. A parsed file is DELETED IMMEDIATELY after reading. requirements.title: Command Code resolves an approval by writing a reply file and records a session grant for always
source_evidence: porting/decision_batch_20260922b.md F1 - every remaining "Droppy Code" / "droppy-code" the app shows or sends out becomes "Marrow" / "marrow", except droppy-code.json and DROPPY_CODE_PROJECT_ROOT (accepted by OD-0012)
requirements.preconditions: A pending approval keyed by requestID.
requirements.expected_result: An unknown id does nothing. For "allow" or "always" the request is allowed; "always" ALSO inserts the row's grant key into the session grants, so every later request of that kind is auto-allowed for the rest of the session. Anything else denies. .requestResolved is emitted. The reply payload is verbatim: {"decision":"allow"} to allow, and {"decision":"deny","reason":"The user declined this in Marrow. Do not retry it; take another approach or explain what you would need."} to deny (OD-0012 F1; upstream "The user declined this in Droppy Code. ..."). It is written to "<id>.reply.json" by writing "<id>.reply.json.tmp" atomically and then replacing the target; if that fails, it falls back to writing the target directly and atomically, with any failure ignored.

requirements.persistence: The reply file is consumed and deleted by the mod.
failure_cases: A failed write leaves the mod polling until the turn ends or its six-hour deadline passes.
requirements.windows_path: The temp-then-replace sequence must be an atomic replace on Windows, because the mod polls the target file and must never read a partial write. A replace can fail while the mod has the file open; the direct-write fallback is what covers that, and it must also be atomic. Before the first reply <id>.reply.json does not exist; the replace then throws (O-35, ED-123), the direct atomic write lands the reply, and <id>.reply.json.tmp remains until clearApprovalFiles removes it.

requirements.title: The Command Code mod sanitizes the call id, writes a request file atomically and polls for a reply every 40 ms
source_evidence: porting/decision_batch_20260922b.md F1 - every remaining "Droppy Code" / "droppy-code" the app shows or sends out becomes "Marrow" / "marrow", except droppy-code.json and DROPPY_CODE_PROJECT_ROOT (accepted by OD-0012)

Otherwise: the id is the toolCallId, or, when absent, `${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}`, with every character outside A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore, period and hyphen replaced by an underscore. Any stale reply file is unlinked. The request is written to "<id>.request.json.tmp" and RENAMED onto "<id>.request.json", carrying {toolCallId: <the sanitized id>, toolName, input}. Then the hook polls: it reads the reply file; when present it unlinks it, parses it (a parse failure yields an empty object), and returns nothing when answer.decision is exactly 'allow', otherwise {block: true, additionalContext: answer.reason || 'The user declined this in Marrow.'} (OD-0012 F1; upstream 'The user declined this in Droppy Code.'). Between polls it sleeps 40 milliseconds.
side_effects: Files written, renamed and deleted; a busy-ish poll loop for the life of the prompt
requirements.persistence: The request file is the channel; the app deletes it as it reads it.
failure_cases: A reply that is not valid JSON blocks the call with the default decline text.
requirements.windows_path: The rename onto an existing name must be an atomic replace on Windows. The sanitized id becomes a FILE NAME, and the allowed character set already excludes every Windows-illegal character, so no additional sanitization is needed or permitted.

requirements.title: The Command Code mod gives up on an abort signal, an orphaned parent or a six-hour deadline

requirements.preconditions: The hook is polling for a reply.
requirements.action: One of the three exit conditions is met.
requirements.expected_result: When ctx.signal.aborted becomes true, the request file is unlinked and the hook returns {block: true, additionalContext: 'The turn was stopped.'} When process.ppid is exactly 1, OR more than 6 * 60 * 60 * 1000 milliseconds have passed since the request was written, the request file is unlinked and the hook returns {block: true, additionalContext: 'Marrow did not answer.'} All three messages are verbatim; the last is the OD-0012 F1 wording (upstream 'Droppy Code did not answer.').

requirements.title: Command Code auth status asks the CLI only when a key exists, and reads three signals out of its output
requirements.preconditions: A resolved executable.
requirements.action: Settings reads the Command Code sign-in state.
requirements.expected_result: With no API key at all the CLI is NOT asked and .signedOut is returned at once. Otherwise Shell.run(executable, ["status", "--no-auto-update"], environment:, timeout: 25) runs; a throw returns .unknown. ANSI is stripped from stdout plus stderr. Then, in order: a regular-expression match of "Authenticated as " followed by one or more non-space characters returns .signedIn with that captured name; an exit status of exactly 3, or text containing "not authenticated" or "not logged in" case-insensitively, returns .signedOut; text containing "authentication verified" case-insensitively returns .signedIn with the stored login's user name, which may be nil; anything else returns .unknown.

requirements.windows_path: ANSI stripping is load-bearing on Windows. The argv is ["status", "--no-auto-update"] on the SAME executable that PR-PROVCLI-203 must validate; running it against the Windows command interpreter would open a console rather than answer. Executable identity is validated per PA-0016: PATH resolution honours PATHEXT, and a candidate whose Windows version resource identifies it as the command interpreter (CompanyName Microsoft Corporation with OriginalFilename Cmd.Exe/Cmd.Exe.MUI, or FileDescription Windows Command Processor), or which is %SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe or %SystemRoot%\SysWOW64\cmd.exe, is rejected and the provider reports not installed.

On a miss the id is split on hyphens, a leading "individual" part is dropped, and an empty remainder yields nil; otherwise each part is mapped: "goat" -> "GOAT", "pro" -> "Pro", "go" -> "Go", "max" -> "Max", "ultra" -> "Ultra", "teams" or "team" -> "Teams", a part matching one or more digits followed by a lowercase x -> those digits plus "×", and anything else -> its first character uppercased followed by the rest unchanged. The parts are joined by single spaces, so an unfamiliar plan never shows as nothing.

requirements.title: Command Code lists models from the CLI's own printed table, keeping one default
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CommandCodeAPI.swift:179-234 - listModels and parseModels with the doc comment
requirements.preconditions: A resolved executable.
requirements.action: The registry loads the Command Code catalog.
requirements.expected_result: Shell.run(executable, ["--list-models", "--no-auto-update"], environment:, timeout: 30) runs and its STDOUT is ANSI-stripped. The user's config.json supplies the configured model from "model" and the configured efforts object from "reasoningEffort". Parsing: each line is trimmed; empty lines are skipped; lines beginning with "Available models", "Pass the full id", "cmd ", "Docs:" or "Usage" are skipped. A line matching one or more non-space characters, then TWO OR MORE spaces, then the rest, is a model row; the id must contain a hyphen or a slash or the row is skipped. The detail is the remainder trimmed, with the literal " (recommended)" and " (default)" substrings REMOVED and each setting its own flag. The option carries id, name = displayName(for: id), detail = the section header and the remaining detail joined by " · " with nils dropped, efforts = efforts(for: id), defaultEffort = the configured efforts object indexed by the id, and isDefault = recommended or CLI-default, further forced true when the id matches the configured model. A non-matching line becomes the current SECTION HEADER when it has no space and starts with an uppercase letter, or when it is shorter than 24 characters. Finally: when a configured model matches a row, every other row's isDefault is cleared and that row is MOVED to index 0; otherwise the first row already marked default becomes the only default and nothing is reordered. An empty result throws ProviderError.failed with the last lines of stderr plus stdout, or the literal "Command Code listed no models."

requirements.expected_result: There is NO initialize. First a request {"type":"get_state"} is sent. Its payload is read from the reply's "data" when present, else from the reply itself. A non-empty "sessionFile" string becomes the session id; failing that, a non-empty "sessionId" string does. The context window is taken from data.model.contextWindow. .sessionReady is emitted with the session id or the EMPTY STRING. Then a request {"type":"get_commands"} is sent, its payload read the same way, and each entry of "commands" with a string "name" becomes a SlashCommand with that name and its "description" or the empty string; a non-empty list is emitted as .commands. Finally started becomes true and stopped false, and start() returns the session id or the empty string.

Otherwise requestCounter is incremented BEFORE use, so the first id is exactly "droppy-1"; the literal prefix is "droppy-", NOT "marrow-" as Claude uses (PR-PROVCLI-019, OD-0012 F1). The id is added to the request object. If the calling task is already cancelled, the call returns JSON null without writing the line, and the id number is still used up. Otherwise the id is registered first and the line is then written. The call returns the whole reply message when a line arrives whose type is "response" and whose id matches. It returns JSON NULL when 30 seconds pass first, when the process closes first (didClose resolves every waiting request with null before anything else, PR-PROVCLI-299), or when the calling task is cancelled while waiting. It NEVER THROWS. The consequence, recorded as an upstream oddity: a hung get_state leaves start() returning an EMPTY session id rather than reporting an error, and the thread then believes it has a session it cannot resume.

requirements.windows_path: None beyond the port's PendingReplies (B3_PLAN.md section 3 N1) with a 30 second timeout whose value is JSON null. The id prefix is a contract with the app's own reader. It is "droppy-", which is neither "Droppy Code" nor "droppy-code", the two spellings OD-0012 F1 renames, so it is kept.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test with a stand-in that never answers get_state, asserting start() returns an empty id after 30 seconds; plus a stand-in that exits while a request waits (null at once), a caller cancelled while waiting (null at once) and a pre-cancelled caller (null, no stdin line, requestCounter advanced)

requirements.title: Pi builds a whole-file unified diff for edits and writes, through a no-op relativization
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiSession.swift:439-466 - editDiff and unifiedDiff with the doc comment; a write's old side is `editSnapshots.text(id)` then `editSnapshots.discard(id)` (:450-451, DroppyCode/Services/Providers/SessionSupport.swift:13-15, :21-23)
requirements.preconditions: A finished edit or write.
requirements.expected_result: For a tool named exactly "edit": a string args.path is required, and the diff is built from args.oldText and args.newText, each defaulting to the empty string. For "write": a string args.path and a string args.content are required, and the old side is the recorded snapshot, REMOVED as it is consumed, defaulting to the empty string. Any other name returns nil. The diff is a header of "--- a/<path>" and "+++ b/<path>" on two lines, then EVERY non-empty line of the old text prefixed with "-", then EVERY non-empty line of the new text prefixed with "+", all joined by single newlines - not a real unified diff with hunks. The additions and deletions come from diffStats. The path is passed through `path.hasPrefix("/") ? path : path`, whose two branches are IDENTICAL, so the ternary is a no-op and the path is NEVER made relative; the FileEdit therefore carries the absolute path.
failure_cases: A missing path or content yields no edits.
requirements.windows_path: The no-op ternary means Pi's file rows show ABSOLUTE paths where the other providers show relative ones, and on Windows those will be drive-letter paths inside a diff header that looks like a POSIX one. This is an upstream defect and is reproduced, not repaired.

When either fails, the request is recorded as a question with method "select" and emitted as a plain .question with header "Pi", the raw title as the prompt, the offered options as choices, allowsOther false and isSecret false. When both succeed, the payload's fields are "kind", "toolName", "toolCallId" and "input", as the extension wrote them.
failure_cases: A malformed payload degrades to a plain question rather than failing.
requirements.windows_path: The prefix test is ordinal and the drop count is measured in characters of that literal.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over a real gate title, a malformed one and an unrelated select

requirements.title: Pi auto-allows a gate request whose kind already holds a session grant
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiSession.swift:557-561 - let kindString = payload["kind"]?.string ?? "tool"; if sessionGrants.contains(kindString) { send extension_ui_response with value "Allow"; return }
requirements.preconditions: A parsed gate payload.
requirements.expected_result: The kind string is payload.kind or the literal "tool". When the session grants already contain that EXACT string, a reply {"type":"extension_ui_response","id":<id>,"value":"Allow"} is written at once - the plain "Allow", not "Allow for session" - and no prompt is shown and no event emitted. The grant keys stored by resolveApproval are exactly "command", "fileChange" and "tool", which match the kinds the extension emits.

failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: None.

requirements.title: Pi gate approvals map three kinds to three row shapes and always offer the same three options
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiSession.swift:562-591 - the kind mapping, the title and detail switch, the three options and the emitted approval
requirements.preconditions: A gate request with no matching session grant.
requirements.expected_result: The tool name is payload.toolName or the literal "tool". The kind is .command for the string "command", .fileChange for "fileChange" and .tool for everything else. The row: .command -> title the unwrapped input.command or the tool name, detail the RAW input.command; .fileChange -> title the relative input.path or the tool name, detail the RAW input.path; .tool and the rest -> title the tool name, detail the PRETTY-printed input unless it is null or compacts to "{}". The options are ALWAYS exactly three, in this order: "allow"/"Approve"/.approve, "always"/"Approve for session"/.approveAlways, "deny"/"Decline"/.decline. The toolItemID is payload.toolCallId. The request is stored as pending under the extension request id and emitted as .approval.
side_effects: One provider event; one pending entry
failure_cases: none
requirements.cancellation: A stop leaves the extension waiting; there is no cancellation reply path.
requirements.windows_path: None.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over all three kinds

requirements.title: Pi's close path first releases every waiting request with JSON null, then ends an active turn and reports an exit with the status and the stderr tail
requirements.preconditions: The process's message stream ended.
requirements.expected_result: FIRST every waiting request is resolved with JSON null (pendingResponses.resolveAll(.null)), so a handshake or model-switch get_state that is still waiting returns at once (PR-PROVCLI-276). Then the stderr tail is taken and the process reference cleared. When a turn was active, it is cleared and .turnCompleted is emitted with .interrupted when interruptRequested, else .failed, carrying the tail as the error when it is non-empty and nil when it is empty. Then, when the session was stopped, the method returns. Otherwise started becomes false and: an exit status of exactly 0 emits .exited(error: nil); any other status emits .exited with "Pi exited with status <status>" plus, when the tail is non-empty, a newline and the tail.
failure_cases: A crash mid-turn reports the turn failed and then the session exited.
requirements.cancellation: A stop suppresses the exit notice but NOT the turn completion, because the turn branch runs before the stopped guard.
requirements.windows_path: The exit status appears verbatim in user-visible text, so a Windows termination code will be shown; the source formats it as a signed integer. The tail comes from the bounded stderr collector (PA-0008).
requirements.verification_method: interaction test over a zero exit, a non-zero exit, a stop mid-turn, and a request waiting at the moment of exit (it returns JSON null)
requirements.b3_note: At 1.7.0 didClose begins with pendingResponses.resolveAll(.null) (PiSession.swift:594), so waiting requests are released before the stderr tail is read and the turn and exit events are emitted.

requirements.title: Pi reports itself running only when started, not stopped and holding a live process
requirements.preconditions: Any state.
requirements.action: The thread asks whether the session is running.
requirements.expected_result: All three must hold: started is true, stopped is false, and the process exists and reports itself running. This is stricter than Command Code, which asks only the two flags, and stricter than Claude, which asks only the process.
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: The process must report not-running promptly after it exits, or send() will attempt a write to a dead pipe.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over each of the three false cases

requirements.title: The Pi gate extension is written as droppy-gate.ts only when its bytes change
requirements.preconditions: A session starting.
requirements.expected_result: The support directory is created with intermediate directories. The file is named exactly "droppy-gate.ts". Its UTF-8 bytes are compared against whatever is on disk and written atomically ONLY when they differ, so a new build's extension replaces the old one. The URL is returned; a write failure propagates.
side_effects: A directory created; possibly one file written
requirements.persistence: The extension file persists between runs.
failure_cases: A failed write throws out of start().
requirements.windows_path: Keep the byte-compare-before-write and the atomic write, because the CLI may be reading the file concurrently (port_impacts.md entry 22).
requirements.verification_method: restart test asserting the file is not rewritten when unchanged

requirements.title: The Pi extension registers MCP tools from the bridge with a middle-dot label and swallows every error
requirements.preconditions: DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE is set.
requirements.expected_result: When the environment key is set the bridge module is imported and AWAITED. For each tool it lists, pi.registerTool is called with name "mcp__" + server + "__" + name, label server + " · " + name (space, U+00B7, space), the tool's description, parameters Type.Unsafe(tool.inputSchema), and an execute function returning { content: [{ type: "text", text }], details: {} }. Any error anywhere in that block is caught and logged to stderr as "droppy mcp: " plus the error's message (or its string form for a non-Error) and otherwise SWALLOWED. Unlike the Command Code mod, this import IS awaited, so tools are registered before the agent runs.
side_effects: Tools registered in the CLI; stderr output on failure
failure_cases: A failing bridge leaves the MCP tools absent, with only a stderr line.
requirements.windows_path: The bridge path is handed to a dynamic import; whether a Windows path works directly or needs a file URL must be probed against the real CLI.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test with a stand-in bridge, and a Windows import-form probe

requirements.title: The Pi extension appends up to three system-prompt segments before the agent starts
requirements.preconditions: The agent is about to start a turn.
requirements.expected_result: The gate is read from the file named by DROPPY_CODE_PI_GATE, or the empty string; ANY throw, including a missing file or malformed JSON, yields an empty object. Three candidate strings are considered IN THIS ORDER: when gate.finalReport is truthy, "Reply with your final report now: no tools, one message."; when gate.interactionMode is exactly "plan", "You are in plan mode: read-only. Do not edit files or run commands that change anything; investigate, then end with the plan as markdown."; when gate.systemPrompt is a string of length greater than zero, that string - a branch that is unreachable in the shipped build. When none applies the hook returns NOTHING and the prompt is untouched. Otherwise the hook returns a system prompt of the event's own prompt, two newlines, and the candidates joined by two newlines.
side_effects: The agent's system prompt is extended
failure_cases: An unreadable gate file silently means no segments are appended, so a plan-mode turn would not be told it is read-only. The tool_call hook's own plan check is what still blocks the tools.
requirements.windows_path: The gate path comes from the environment and is read with a plain filesystem read.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture driving the real extension text with each gate shape

requirements.title: The Pi extension's tool_call hook applies an eight-step decision ladder in a fixed order
requirements.preconditions: A tool is about to run.
requirements.expected_result: The gate is re-read on EVERY call. The ladder, in this exact order: (1) gate.finalReport truthy blocks with reason "Final report: no tools"; (2) a tool name in the four-element read-only set read, grep, find, ls is ALLOWED, even in plan mode and even during a final report - note step 1 is tested before this, so a final report blocks even a read; (3) gate.interactionMode exactly "plan" blocks with reason "Plan mode is read-only"; (4) gate.runtimeMode exactly "fullAccess" allows; (5) the kind is computed as "command" for the tool name "bash", "fileChange" for "edit" or "write", and "tool" otherwise; (6) a fileChange under runtimeMode "autoAcceptEdits" or "auto" allows; (7) a command under runtimeMode "auto" whose input.command is read-only allows; (8) otherwise the user is asked. All the mode comparisons are against the camelCase raw values.
failure_cases: An unreadable gate yields an empty object, so every step falls through to asking the user - the safe answer.
requirements.windows_path: The camelCase mode strings are the on-disk contract described in PR-PROVCLI-277.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture driving the real extension text through every rung of the ladder

requirements.title: The Pi extension classifies a shell command as read-only by splitting on four separators and checking every segment
source_evidence: porting/unknowns.md UNK-0005 (RESOLVED by OD-0008 C5, decision_batch_20260922.md C5)
requirements.preconditions: An Auto-mode command call.
requirements.expected_result: The command is coerced to a string (a nullish value becomes the empty string) and split on the regular expression matching "&&", "||", ";" or "|". EVERY segment must qualify. A segment is trimmed and split on whitespace with empties dropped; a segment with NO words qualifies. A segment whose first word is exactly "git" qualifies only when it has a second word in the six-element set status, diff, log, show, branch, blame. Otherwise the first word must be in the eighteen-element set, in source order: ls, cat, head, tail, grep, rg, find, wc, pwd, echo, which, stat, file, du, tree, sort, uniq, diff. Note this list has no path handling, so a command written as "/bin/ls" does NOT qualify.
failure_cases: Anything not provably read-only is asked, which is the safe answer.
requirements.windows_path: These are Unix tool names, but the classifier runs on the COMMAND TEXT THE MODEL PRODUCED inside the CLI, so the list is a product constant and is copied verbatim. UNK-0005 is marked RESOLVED by OD-0008 C5 ("PowerShell 7 when installed, otherwise Windows PowerShell"), but C5 rules only which shell the app's own terminal tabs and project scripts use; this classifier runs inside the Pi extension on commands Pi itself executes, so C5 does not change it. If a Windows-hosted Pi produces Windows command text, this classifier simply asks more often, which is safe.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture driving the real extension text over a pipeline, a git subcommand, an unknown binary and an empty segment

requirements.title: The Pi extension truncates long string inputs at twenty thousand characters before asking
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiCLI.swift:206-209 - the input copy with the 20000-character slice
requirements.preconditions: The hook has decided to ask.
requirements.expected_result: A fresh object is built from the event's input (or an empty object): every value that is a string LONGER than 20000 characters is replaced by its first 20000 characters; every other value is copied unchanged, including nested objects, which are NOT recursed into. Only top-level string values are truncated.
failure_cases: A large nested object still reaches the select title in full.
requirements.windows_path: The measure is JavaScript string length, which counts UTF-16 code units, so a slice can split a surrogate pair; that is the shipped behavior and is reproduced.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture with a 25000-character string input

requirements.title: The Pi extension asks over a select whose title is a droppy-gate prefix and a JSON payload
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiCLI.swift:210-213 - the payload, the select call and the block reason
requirements.preconditions: The ladder reached the ask step.
requirements.expected_result: The payload is { kind, toolName, toolCallId, input } in that written order. An answer of exactly "Allow" or exactly "Allow for session" returns undefined, allowing the call. Anything else, including a cancellation, blocks with the reason "The user declined this " followed by "command" for a command kind, "file change" for a fileChange kind and "tool call" otherwise.
failure_cases: Any non-allow answer blocks.
requirements.cancellation: A cancelled question blocks the call.
requirements.windows_path: The decline reason's prefix is what the app's handleToolEnd matches to show the row as declined (PR-PROVCLI-292); the two must change together.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture asserting the title, the options and all three reason suffixes

requirements.title: Pi's config directory honours PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR and otherwise sits under the home directory
requirements.preconditions: An environment.
requirements.expected_result: When PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR is set and non-empty, that path is used verbatim as a directory URL. Otherwise the home is environment["HOME"] when non-empty, else LoginEnvironment.homeDirectory, and the directory is that home joined with the literal segment ".pi/agent".
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: HOME is normally unset on Windows, so LoginEnvironment.homeDirectory carries this and must resolve to the user profile. The segment uses a forward slash and must be joined as path components.
requirements.verification_method: unit test with and without the environment variable

requirements.title: Pi auth status reports the sorted provider names from auth.json, else any of eight environment keys
requirements.preconditions: A config directory.
requirements.action: Settings reads the Pi sign-in state.
requirements.expected_result: <config>/auth.json is read. When it parses to a NON-EMPTY object, .signedIn is returned with that object's KEYS SORTED and joined by ", " - the keys are provider names such as anthropic and openai. Otherwise the environment is checked, in this exact order, for a non-empty value under ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY, MISTRAL_API_KEY, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, XAI_API_KEY; the FIRST hit returns .signedIn with a NIL account name. With neither, .signedOut. This reader never returns .unknown and never runs a process.
failure_cases: An unreadable or empty auth file falls through to the environment check.
requirements.windows_path: The sort must be ordinal so the displayed order is stable. Environment variable names are case-insensitive on Windows, so a differently-cased key would also be found, which is a small behavioural widening the port should note.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over a populated auth file, an empty one, each environment key and none

requirements.title: Pi's catalog probe launches an eight-token throwaway process in the home directory
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiCLI.swift:46-64 - listModels launch, environment and the two fixed-id requests
requirements.preconditions: A resolved executable.

requirements.expected_result: The working directory is the resolved home - environment["HOME"] when non-empty, else LoginEnvironment.homeDirectory. The environment is the caller's plus PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK = "1", and NOTHING else; the gate and MCP keys are not set here. The argv is exactly these 8 tokens: "--mode", "rpc", "--no-session", "--no-extensions", "--no-skills", "--no-prompt-templates", "--no-themes", "--no-context-files". Framing is .lines. A start failure throws ProviderError.failed("Pi could not start: " plus the localized description). Two lines are written with FIXED LITERAL ids, not the droppy- counter: {"type":"get_state","id":"state"} and {"type":"get_available_models","id":"models"}.
failure_cases: The prefixed start message above.
requirements.cancellation: A 30 second timer terminates the process (PR-PROVCLI-311).

requirements.verification_method: contract fixture asserting the argv and both request lines

requirements.title: Pi's catalog probe reads until both replies arrive or thirty seconds pass, then terminates
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiCLI.swift:65-83 - the two response slots, the 30 second timeout task, the read loop breaking when both are present, then timeout.cancel() and process.terminate()
requirements.preconditions: The probe started.
requirements.expected_result: Each inbound message is filed by its "id": the literal "state" or the literal "models"; anything else is ignored. The loop breaks as soon as BOTH have arrived. A detached Task sleeps exactly 30 seconds and then terminates the process unconditionally - note it does NOT check for cancellation first, unlike Claude's and Codex's watchdogs, so a late cancel races the terminate harmlessly. After the loop the timer is cancelled and the process terminated again.
failure_cases: A timeout ends the stream with one or both replies missing, which produces the no-models error.
requirements.windows_path: terminate() is TerminateProcess; the probe persists nothing so that is acceptable.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test with a stand-in that answers only one request

requirements.title: Pi's catalog maps models to provider-slash-id options sorted by provider then name
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiCLI.swift:85-112 - the mapping, the current-model test, the empty-list throw and the sort
requirements.preconditions: Both probe replies arrived.
requirements.expected_result: The state payload is stateResponse.data, else the response itself, else JSON null; the current provider and id come from its model.provider and model.id. The items come from modelsResponse.data.models, else modelsResponse.models, else the empty array. Each item needs a string "provider" and a string "id"; reasoning is item.reasoning being exactly true. The option id is "<provider>/<id>", the name is item.name or the id, the detail is the PROVIDER string, the efforts are the seven thinking levels when reasoning and the empty array otherwise, and the default effort is the literal "medium" when reasoning and nil otherwise. isDefault is true when a current provider and id are both known AND either the current id contains a slash and equals the full id, or it does not and the provider and id match separately. An EMPTY result throws ProviderError.failed("Pi listed no models.") verbatim. The list is finally sorted by the pair (detail or the empty string, name) - that is, by provider then name.
failure_cases: The exact message above.
requirements.windows_path: The sort compares strings; it must be ordinal so the catalog order is stable across locales.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over a reasoning model, a non-reasoning model, both current-id shapes and an empty list

requirements.title: Pi plan limits read only the OAuth logins Pi holds, skipping non-oauth and expired entries
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiPlanLimits.swift:10-41 - read(environment:) with the doc comment at :3-5 and the expiry comment at :22
requirements.preconditions: A config directory.
requirements.action: The usage panel reads Pi's limits.
requirements.expected_result: <config>/auth.json is read and must parse to an object, else nil. Its keys are walked SORTED. An entry is skipped unless its "type" is exactly "oauth" AND its "access" is a non-empty string. An entry whose "expires" is a double is skipped when that value, read as epoch MILLISECONDS, is already in the past - an expired token buys nothing from the usage endpoint. Then the key decides the reader: exactly "anthropic" reads the Anthropic usage endpoint; exactly "openai-codex" OR exactly "openai" reads the Codex one; EVERY OTHER KEY IS SKIPPED. A nil result from a reader is skipped. Surviving windows are appended in key order and surviving plan names collected. With no windows at all the result is nil; otherwise a PlanLimits whose plan name is the collected names joined by " · " (space, U+00B7, space), or nil when none were collected.
side_effects: READS A THIRD-PARTY CREDENTIAL FILE. Pi's <config>/auth.json holds the OAuth access tokens of the providers Pi is signed into, and those tokens are then sent to Anthropic's and OpenAI's usage endpoints. Up to two network requests carrying a third party's bearer token.
requirements.persistence: The registry persists the plan limits.
failure_cases: No usable logins: nil.
requirements.cancellation: Each request has its own 15 second timeout.
requirements.windows_path: PLATFORM BOUNDARY. The key sort must be ordinal. The file is read directly from the CLI's own config directory and the app never writes it. The read, and the requests that carry Pi's tokens to the Anthropic and Codex usage endpoints (PR-PROVCLI-314, PR-PROVCLI-315), are reproduced as upstream: BLK-0007 is RESOLVED by OD-0008 (decision batch A7, "Keep as upstream (it is how the plan-limit feature works)"), ruling: "REPRODUCE UPSTREAM: plan limits read each CLI's own credential file and query that provider's usage endpoint exactly as the source does. Parity, owner-approved." Treated identically to PR-PROVREG-177, PR-PROVREG-121 and PR-PROVCLI-255.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over an expired token, a non-oauth entry, an unknown provider key and two live ones

requirements.title: Pi reads Anthropic usage with a beta header and prefixes the plan name with Claude
requirements.preconditions: A live anthropic OAuth token.
requirements.expected_result: A 15 second request to https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage carrying Authorization "Bearer <token>", anthropic-beta "oauth-2025-04-20" and Accept "application/json". Anything but HTTP 200, or an unparseable body, yields nil. The body is parsed by PlanLimitsReader.parseClaudeUsage with limits from json.limits (or the empty array), a nil plan name and the titlePrefix "Claude"; a nil result yields nil. The plan name is then OVERWRITTEN with json.subscription_type mapped through PlanLimitsReader.planName and prefixed "Claude ", or, when either step yields nothing, the bare literal "Claude".
requirements.persistence: Part of the persisted plan limits.
failure_cases: A non-200 or unparseable response yields nil for this provider only.
requirements.windows_path: Network only.
requirements.verification_method: unit test against a recorded response with and without a subscription_type

requirements.title: Pi reads Codex usage with an account id taken from the token's own claim
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiPlanLimits.swift:8,:59-79 - codexUsageURL and readCodex with the comment at :64
requirements.preconditions: A live openai-codex or openai OAuth token.
requirements.expected_result: A 15 second request to https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage carrying Authorization "Bearer <token>" and Accept "application/json". When an account id can be extracted and is non-empty, the header "ChatGPT-Account-Id" carries it. The account id comes from the token's SECOND dot-separated part decoded as base64url: hyphens become plus, underscores become slash, and the string is padded with equals signs to a multiple of four; the decoded JSON's field at the path "https://api.openai.com/auth" then "chatgpt_account_id" is the id. A token with fewer than two parts, or one that fails to decode or parse, yields no id and the header is omitted. Anything but HTTP 200, or an unparseable body, yields nil. The rate limit object is json.rate_limit, else the whole body. Two windows are built from "primary_window" and "secondary_window"; with none, nil. The plan name is json.plan_type mapped through PlanLimitsReader.codexPlanName and prefixed "Codex ", or the bare literal "Codex".
requirements.persistence: Part of the persisted plan limits.
failure_cases: A malformed token simply omits the header, which may make the endpoint answer for the wrong scope or refuse.
requirements.windows_path: Base64 decoding must be strict about the padding rule described; a decoder that rejects unpadded input would break the header. No credential is ever written anywhere.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over a token with and without the claim, plus a recorded usage response

requirements.title: Pi's Codex windows require a used percent and a window length, and derive a reset time two ways
requirements.preconditions: A rate-limit window object.
requirements.expected_result: The window is nil unless the raw value exists AND carries a double "used_percent" AND an int "limit_window_seconds". The reset time is Date(timeIntervalSince1970:) of "reset_at" when that is a double; otherwise, when "reset_after_seconds" is an int, it is that many seconds from NOW; otherwise nil. The id is the literal passed in, exactly "codex-primary" or "codex-secondary". The title is the literal "Codex · " (space, U+00B7, space) followed by PlanLimitsReader.windowTitle(minutes: limit_window_seconds / 60) - an INTEGER division, so a window shorter than sixty seconds titles as zero minutes. The percent is used_percent unchanged, with NO clamping.
requirements.persistence: Part of the persisted plan limits.
failure_cases: A missing percent or window length drops that window silently.
requirements.windows_path: None.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over both reset shapes, a sub-minute window and a missing percent

requirements.title: Antigravity's executable is agy with no fallback paths, and a missing one is reported as not installed

With none, start() throws ProviderError.notInstalled(.antigravity), described exactly as "Antigravity is not installed. Install it and sign in with `agy`." - the login command is the bare "agy".

requirements.title: Antigravity's base argument vector is eight tokens ending in an explicit workspace directory
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/AntigravitySession.swift:72-81 - the comment plus the literal array

The print timeout's value is the literal STRING "30m". The comment records why --add-dir is required: the CLI does not adopt its cwd, verified live and in both a git repository and not, so without the flag the agent works in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/scratch and spends its first steps hunting the home directory for the project.

requirements.title: Antigravity passes each connected MCP server id as its own argv token, sorted
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/AntigravitySession.swift:82-84 - the comment plus let connected = MCPProviderConfig.connectedIDs(); if !connected.isEmpty { arguments += ["--allowed-mcp-server-names"] + connected }
DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPProviderConfig.swift:230-236 - connectedIDs() returns the mcpServers keys sorted, or the empty array
requirements.preconditions: MCP settings may or may not have connected servers.
requirements.expected_result: With no connected servers NOTHING is appended. Otherwise ONE flag token "--allowed-mcp-server-names" is appended followed by EVERY id as its OWN separate token - not a comma-joined or space-joined single value. The ids come back SORTED, or the empty array when the config file is missing or its object empty, so the order is deterministic and lexicographic. Only the connected servers are allowed for the session, so the user's own stay out of it without being touched.
failure_cases: No file or an empty object: no flag at all.
requirements.windows_path: The ids must stay as separate argv elements or Windows command-line quoting will mangle them into one (port_impacts.md entry 25). The sort must be ordinal.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture with three connected servers asserting four separate tokens

retired.reason: At B2 Antigravity passes no MCP argv token at all. source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/AntigravitySession.swift:88-90 - let (resolvedModel, resolvedEffort) = Self.normalize(model: model, effort: effort); if let resolvedModel, !resolvedModel.isEmpty { arguments += ["--model", resolvedModel] }; if let resolvedEffort, !resolvedEffort.isEmpty { arguments += ["--effort", resolvedEffort] }
requirements.preconditions: A model and an effort, either possibly nil.
requirements.expected_result: A nil or EMPTY model returns (nil, nil), so NEITHER --model nor --effort is passed whatever the effort setting. Otherwise the slug is parsed: a trailing "-high", "-medium" or "-low" is stripped, TESTED IN THAT ORDER, and the matching " (High)", " (Medium)" or " (Low)" suffix stripped from the display name, yielding a base slug and a parsed effort. A base slug CONTAINING the substring "claude" returns (baseSlug, nil), so such a model gets --model and NO --effort. Otherwise the effort is resolved in this precedence: the explicit effort argument; then the effort parsed out of the slug suffix; then a default of "medium" for the exact slug "gpt-oss-120b" and "high" for everything else. Then two hard overrides are applied AFTER the default: the exact slug "gemini-3.1-pro" with effort "medium" becomes "high"; the exact slug "gpt-oss-120b" is ALWAYS forced to "medium", overriding even an explicit high or low. The resulting model appends "--model" and its value when non-empty; the resulting effort appends "--effort" and its value when non-empty. The only literal model identifiers compared are the substring "claude" and the exact slugs "gemini-3.1-pro" and "gpt-oss-120b". The CLI accepts exactly three efforts: low, medium, high.

requirements.windows_path: The substring and equality tests are ordinal.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over an empty model, a claude slug, gpt-oss-120b with an explicit high, gemini-3.1-pro with medium, and a slug carrying a -low suffix

requirements.title: Antigravity reads plan limits from two zero-token headless calls and never reports a plan name
requirements.preconditions: A resolved executable.

Until one unknown shared by PR-PROVCLI-105, PR-PROVCLI-173 and PR-PROVCLI-341 is registered and settled, only the Z-suffixed shapes and the rejection of junk are specified, and the port must not claim parity for any other input.

source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:301-309 control(_:) - `controlCounter += 1` / `let requestID = "droppy-code-\(controlCounter)"` / `return try await pendingControl.register(requestID) {` / `process.send(["type": "control_request", "request_id": .string(requestID), "request": request])`

DroppyCode/Core/Support/PendingReplies.swift:10-36 register - `try Task.checkCancellation()` comes before the continuation is stored and `send()` runs (:17-20); on cancellation `self?.continuations.removeValue(forKey: id)?.resume(throwing: CancellationError())` runs in a main-actor task (:31-34)
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ClaudeSession.swift:336-341 - a control_response that arrives later for that id finds no waiting entry (PendingReplies.swift:38-50 return false) and is dropped
requirements.preconditions: A control request (initialize, set_permission_mode, set_model, interrupt, stop_task) is made from a task that is, or becomes, cancelled.
requirements.expected_result: The process and hasClosed checks come first (PR-PROVCLI-019); then controlCounter is advanced and the id is built. If the calling task is already cancelled, control(_:) throws CancellationError before anything is stored or written: no control_request line is sent, and that id number is used up, so the next request's id skips it. Otherwise the id is registered before the line is sent. If the calling task is cancelled while the reply is outstanding, the waiting entry is removed and the caller resumes by throwing CancellationError, and a control_response that arrives later for that id is dropped; a reply delivered before the cancellation takes effect is returned to the caller as usual. No timeout applies: a caller that is neither cancelled nor answered waits until the reply arrives or didClose fails it. This holds for every control() caller, start()'s initialize included.
side_effects: A request cancelled before the send advances controlCounter without writing to stdin
failure_cases: Cancelled before the send: CancellationError, nothing sent, the id skipped
Cancelled while waiting: CancellationError, and the late reply is dropped
requirements.cancellation: Cancellable before the send and while waiting, as described; the removal on cancellation runs as a separate main-actor task.
requirements.windows_path: Use the port's PendingReplies (the C# counterpart of Core/Support/PendingReplies.swift, B3_PLAN.md section 3 N1) keyed by the "marrow-<n>" id (OD-0012 F1): check for cancellation before registering and sending, and on cancellation remove the entry and fail the waiter with the port's cancellation error.
requirements.verification_method: unit with a fake process: a pre-cancelled caller throws CancellationError, no stdin line is written and the next request id is two higher; a caller cancelled while waiting throws CancellationError and a later reply for its id changes nothing; a reply that arrives before the cancellation is returned

requirements.preconditions: A provider session (Pi, Command Code or Antigravity) is streaming one assistant turn and holds one StreamedTextTracker (Swift: `var stream`) for it.
requirements.action: The session calls the tracker's mutating methods as the turn's stream events arrive: startMessage/appendMessage for message text, startThinking/appendThinking for reasoning text, and endThinking/endMessage/resetThinking/resetForTurn/resetIDs to close or clear state.
requirements.expected_result: startMessage always mints a fresh message id (messageCounter incremented, id built from it), empties messageText and clears streamedText. appendMessage mints an id only when none is current (the first delta of a turn); otherwise it keeps the current id. Every appendMessage call sets streamedText true and appends the delta to messageText, so a later call accumulates onto the existing buffer. startThinking always mints a fresh thinking id and empties thinkingText. appendThinking mints an id only when none is current: resetsText true (the default, Pi's fallback) does so by calling startThinking, which also empties thinkingText; resetsText false (Command Code's fallback) mints the id directly without clearing thinkingText, so text already accumulated survives. Every appendThinking call, on either path, appends the delta to thinkingText. endThinking and endMessage each clear only their own current id, leaving the accumulated text untouched. resetThinking clears both currentThinkingID and thinkingText together (a message_start that interrupts an in-progress reasoning block drops it). resetForTurn clears only streamedText, leaving ids and text alone. resetIDs clears both currentMessageID and currentThinkingID but leaves messageText, thinkingText and streamedText untouched.
side_effects: messageCounter and thinkingCounter are monotonically incremented counters that never reset, so minted ids stay unique across a session's turns
requirements.cancellation: not cancellable (every method is a synchronous, in-memory state mutation with no suspension point).
requirements.windows_path: Ported verbatim as the sealed class StreamedTextTracker in src/Marrow.Services/Providers/SessionSupport.cs (:45-124, unit N7): Func<long,string> delegates for messageID/thinkingID (Swift `(Int) -> String`), long counters for messageCounter/thinkingCounter (Swift Int), and get-only properties for CurrentMessageID/CurrentThinkingID/MessageText/ThinkingText/StreamedText mirroring the Swift private(set) vars. Shared by every session that adopts SessionSupport; Pi, Command Code and Antigravity keep their own inlined copies until their own lanes switch them over (this unit, lane L2b, only adds the shared type).
requirements.verification_method: unit test per method: StartMessage mints a fresh id, clears the buffer and streamedText; AppendMessage mints an id only when none is current and always sets streamedText, keeping the current id and accumulating text on a later call; StartThinking mints a fresh id and clears thinkingText; AppendThinking exercises both resetsText branches (true starts fresh and clears the buffer, false mints an id without clearing it); EndThinking and EndMessage clear only the current id; ResetThinking clears both the current id and the reasoning text; ResetForTurn clears only the streamedText flag; ResetIDs clears both current ids but not the accumulated text
requirements.b3_note: New at B3 (unit N7): SessionSupport.swift is a new file at 1.7.0, gathering StreamedTextTracker verbatim out of the Pi, Command Code and Antigravity sessions' own inlined copies (Pi PiSession.swift:37-44, 57, 310-316, 346-405, 496-500; CommandCodeSession.swift:42-50, 293-337, 438-439, 629-646; AntigravitySession.swift:47, 232, 259-273); those three files keep their own inlined copies until their own lanes adopt this shared type.

requirements.title: EditSnapshots captures a file's before-text when a tool call starts and reports the finished edit as before/after text, or as a no-diff edit when the file did not change, when the call finishes
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/SessionSupport.swift:27-33 finish(_:path:relativeTo:) - `guard let before = contents.removeValue(forKey: id) else { return nil }` / `let relative = ToolTitles.relativePath(path, to: root)` / `let after = Self.read(path) ?? ""` / `guard before != after else { return [FileEdit(path: relative)] }` / `return [FileEdit(path: relative, old: before, new: after)]`
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/SessionSupport.swift:13-19 discard(_:) removes a snapshot without finishing it; removeAll() clears every snapshot

DroppyCode/Services/Providers/SessionSupport.swift:36-40 read(_:) - a file over 1,000,000 bytes, or one resourceValues(forKeys: [.fileSizeKey]) cannot stat or String(contentsOf:encoding:) cannot decode as UTF-8, reads as nil
requirements.preconditions: A tool call that edits a file (a provider session's edit/write tool) is about to run, and the session holds one EditSnapshots (Swift: `var edits`) across the call.
requirements.action: capture(_:path:) is called as the tool call starts; finish(_:path:relativeTo:) is called when it completes. discard/removeAll/text are used elsewhere to drop a pending snapshot, clear all of them, or read a snapshot's captured text without finishing it.
requirements.expected_result: capture reads the file's current text and stores it keyed by the call's id; a file that read(_:) returns nil for (missing, over 1 MB, or undecodable as UTF-8) is stored as empty string, so a call that then writes a brand-new file reports a whole-file addition rather than failing to find a before-text. finish removes and returns that stored before-text; if the id has no stored snapshot (never captured, or already finished/discarded) it returns nil and the row's edits list is left as already queued. Otherwise it re-reads the file's current text as after (again empty if unreadable), turns path into a root-relative path (ToolTitles.relativePath), and if before and after are equal by Swift's canonical `!=` comparison it returns a single FileEdit with no diff; otherwise it returns a single FileEdit carrying both before and after text. discard drops a snapshot without producing a FileEdit. removeAll drops every pending snapshot. text returns the id's captured text, or empty string if nothing was captured for it, without removing it.
side_effects: capture and finish/discard mutate the shared `contents` dictionary keyed by call id, so a session must not reuse a call id across two in-flight snapshots
failure_cases: finish for an id with no stored snapshot returns nil rather than throwing or fabricating text
a file that cannot be read (missing, larger than 1 MB, or not valid UTF-8) is treated as empty string on both capture and finish, not as an error
requirements.cancellation: not cancellable (capture/finish each do a single synchronous file read; no suspension point).
requirements.windows_path: Ported as the sealed class EditSnapshots in src/Marrow.Services/Providers/SessionSupport.cs (:16-44, unit N7), backed by a Dictionary<string,string> keyed with SwiftStringComparer.Instance (:18) rather than plain ordinal string keys, matching Swift's canonical Dictionary<String,String> key equality. Read(path) (:36-40) checks FileInfo.Exists/Length instead of Swift's resourceValues(forKeys: [.fileSizeKey]), and decodes with SwiftText.DecodeUtf8OrNil over File.ReadAllBytes instead of Foundation's String(contentsOf:encoding:), matching this port's established UTF-8-decode convention (keeps a literal U+FEFF for a BOM, unlike Encoding.UTF8's reader/writer defaults) rather than a plain File.ReadAllText call. Finish's before/after comparison uses SwiftString.Equal, not C#'s ordinal ==, to match Swift's canonical `!=` (:31).
requirements.verification_method: unit test per behavior: capture+finish with no change returns a single no-diff FileEdit; capture+finish with a change returns the before/after FileEdit; finish for an uncaptured id returns null; finish reports a path relative to the given root; capture of a missing file and of a file over 1 MB both read as empty so a subsequent write shows as a whole-file addition; discard removes a snapshot without finishing it; removeAll clears every snapshot; text returns the captured text or empty string; and a dedicated test pins Swift canonical string equality (precomposed vs. decomposed accented character), not ordinal ==, for the before/after comparison in finish

states: Present on every item/permissions/requestApproval, as one of a FIXED three-option list that is never filtered
interactions: click - option id "turn"; answers with the originally requested permission object and scope "turn"
ui.notes: Note the wording differs from every other approve button in the area, which read "Approve". This card is the only place "Allow once" appears.
